abstract: Biological membranes are complex structural and functional assemblies that play central roles in many cellular processes. They are primarily composed of lipids and proteins, whose dynamics and interactions are commonly investigated at the molecular level using Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations. Local membrane curvature, arising from changes in lipid composition and lipid-protein interactions, is an important property linked to lipid and protein sorting as well as protein mechanisms of action. Here, we present MembraneCurvature, a fast, user-friendly, and fully documented Python package designed to compute membrane curvature from MD simulations. Using selected lipid atoms as a reference, MembraneCurvature derives membrane surfaces and calculates molecular descriptors such as mean and Gaussian curvature. The package is built on top of the MDAnalysis library, a versatile framework compatible with simulations obtained from different software, force fields and membranes of simple or complex compositions. To demonstrate its application, we analyze MD simulations of a model plasma membrane generated using the Martini force field, both in the presence and absence of the phospholipid efflux ABC transporter ABCA1. In this example, MembraneCurvature identifies persistent, protein-induced membrane curvature that depends on the protein's conformational state and that is leaflet-specific.
